candidateAdjudication.relation: The revised cleavage card asks for the general diagnostic property: breaking along specific planes, often at fixed orientations/angles. Mica-sheets asks which mineral splits into thin shiny sheets and keys mica. The first is a general break-pattern property definition; the second identifies a specific sheet silicate from its characteristic habit/cleavage. They share a geological concept but no longer test the same mica↔cleavage mapping in opposite directions.
candidateAdjudication.sourceReview: I extracted and read Earle, Physical Geology, printed pages 43–44 (PDF pages 52–53) from the preserved original PDF. Page 52 states cleavage/fracture describe how minerals break, defines cleavage as breaking along specific planes, and notes diagnostic importance. Page 53 discusses fixed orientations, atomic arrangement and lattice weaknesses, gives mica parallel-sheet planes, feldspar cleavages at 90 degrees, and cleavage as a reliable diagnostic property. This supports the revised general cleavage relation and the mica-specific relation as distinct levels of fact.

passages: Cleavage is what we see when a mineral breaks along a specific plane or planes, while fracture is an irregular break.

The way that minerals break is determined by their atomic arrangement and specifically by the orientation of weaknesses within the lattice. Graphite and the micas, for example, have cleavage planes parallel to their sheets; ... feldspar has two cleavages at 90° to each other.
... cleavage ... is a reliable diagnostic property for most minerals.
